body:
2026年9月5日，美国阳翥道教协会（Yangzhu Taoist Association of America）成立一周年暨道教文化交流活动在纽约 Pier 57 举行。来自纽约州政府、联合国宗教类非政府组织、跨宗教机构及不同宗教团体的嘉宾与各界朋友齐聚一堂，共同庆祝协会成立一周年，并通过道教文化分享、宗教用品展示及文化体验等形式，促进道教在美国的传播以及不同宗教、不同文化之间的交流。

本次周年庆获得美国联邦、纽约州及纽约市不同层面的关注与祝贺。美国总统 Donald J. Trump 此前为美国阳翥道教协会成立一周年活动发来贺卡，向协会及周年庆活动致以祝贺。

纽约州州长 Kathy Hochul 特别指定纽约州州务院信仰与非营利发展服务办公室（Office of Faith & Nonprofit Development Services）主任 Caura Richardson 代表州长出席活动。活动期间，Caura Richardson 当场宣读纽约州州长为美国阳翥道教协会成立一周年发来的贺信，并正式向协会颁发。

与此同时，纽约市市长 Zohran Mamdani 亦为美国阳翥道教协会成立一周年发来正式贺信，对协会在社区参与、文化教育、道教传统传播以及促进不同信仰群体相互理解等方面开展的工作给予肯定，并代表纽约市向协会成立一周年致以祝贺。

至此，美国阳翥道教协会成为首个获得美国联邦、纽约州及纽约市三个层级祝贺与肯定的道教组织。来自联邦、州、市三个层面的祝贺，也体现了美国社会各界对道教文化传播、宗教多元与跨信仰交流的进一步关注。

出席本次活动的重要嘉宾还包括联合国宗教类非政府组织委员会（Committee of Religious NGOs at the United Nations，CRNGO）联席主席、世界瑜伽社区（World Yoga Community）主席 Guruji Dileepkumar Thankappan；纽约跨宗教中心（Interfaith Center of New York，ICNY）项目主任 Henry Goldschmidt；圆佛教（Won Buddhism）首席教务 Rev. Doyeon Park 等。多位嘉宾在活动中致辞，对美国阳翥道教协会成立一周年表示祝贺，并就宗教交流、社区合作以及不同信仰之间增进理解与合作表达支持。

美国阳翥道教协会会长吉法新在致辞中回顾了协会成立一年来的发展。他表示，协会成立的初心，是希望建立一个让更多人认识道教、了解道教、走近道教的平台，让这一传承千年的中国本土宗教传统在现代社会继续得到传承和发展。

过去一年，美国阳翥道教协会从纽约出发，积极开展道教宗教与文化活动，服务信众、传播道教文化，并积极参与社区、政府、跨宗教以及联合国和国际交流平台，与来自不同文化和宗教传统的机构及人士建立交流与合作，让道教的声音出现在越来越多公共及国际交流平台之上。

活动现场还设置了道教法衣、法器及相关宗教用品展示，并举行道教文化知识分享、道教养生体验、传统香囊制作及共同祈福等活动。与会嘉宾和参与者通过现场展示、讲解和亲身体验，对道教的宗教信仰、文化传统及宗教实践有了更加直观的认识。

美国阳翥道教协会表示，成立一周年既是对过去一年发展的回顾，也是新的起点。未来，协会将继续立足纽约，推动道教宗教传承与文化传播，加强与政府、国际组织、宗教团体、跨宗教机构及社会各界的交流合作，让更多人认识道教、了解道教，进一步推动道教在美国及国际社会的交流与发展。

body_en:
On September 5, 2026, the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America held its First Anniversary Celebration and Taoist Cultural Exchange Event at Pier 57 in New York City. Guests and friends from the New York State government, religious NGOs within the United Nations community, interfaith institutions, and diverse religious organizations gathered to celebrate the Association’s first anniversary. Through Taoist cultural presentations, displays of religious items, and interactive cultural activities, the event promoted greater awareness of Taoism in the United States and encouraged dialogue among different religions and cultures.

The anniversary celebration received attention and congratulations from different levels of government in the United States, including the federal, New York State, and New York City levels. President Donald J. Trump had previously sent a congratulatory card recognizing the first anniversary of the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America and extending his congratulations to the Association and its anniversary celebration.

New York State Governor Kathy Hochul designated Caura Richardson, Director of the New York State Department of State’s Office of Faith & Nonprofit Development Services, to represent the Governor at the celebration. During the event, Richardson formally read aloud a congratulatory citation from Governor Hochul recognizing the first anniversary of the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America and presented it to the Association.

At the same time, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also sent an official congratulatory letter recognizing the first anniversary of the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America. The letter acknowledged the Association’s work in community engagement, cultural education, the promotion of Taoist traditions, and fostering greater understanding among different faith communities, while extending congratulations on behalf of the City of New York.

With these recognitions, the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America became the first Taoist organization to receive congratulations and recognition at the federal, New York State, and New York City levels. These expressions of recognition from all three levels also reflected growing attention to Taoist cultural outreach, religious diversity, and interfaith engagement within American society.

Distinguished guests attending the celebration also included Guruji Dileepkumar Thankappan, Co-Chair of the Committee of Religious NGOs at the United Nations (CRNGO) and President of the World Yoga Community; Henry Goldschmidt, Program Director of the Interfaith Center of New York (ICNY); and Rev. Doyeon Park, Chief Chaplain of Won Buddhism, among others. Several guests delivered remarks congratulating the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America on its first anniversary and expressed their support for religious dialogue, community cooperation, and greater understanding and collaboration among different faith traditions.

In his remarks, Dpr. Zhouxinyu Ji, President of the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America, reflected on the Association’s development during its first year. He stated that the Association was founded with the goal of creating a platform through which more people could discover, understand, and engage with Taoism, allowing this indigenous Chinese religious tradition, with thousands of years of history, to continue to be transmitted and developed in contemporary society.

Over the past year, the Yangzhu Taoist Association of America has worked from its base in New York to organize Taoist religious and cultural activities, serve the Taoist community, and promote Taoist culture. The Association has also actively participated in community, governmental, interfaith, United Nations, and international platforms, establishing relationships and cooperation with institutions and individuals from diverse cultural and religious traditions and bringing Taoist perspectives to an increasing number of public and international forums.

The celebration also featured displays of Taoist ceremonial robes, ritual implements, and other religious items, as well as presentations on Taoist culture, Taoist health and wellness practices, traditional sachet-making activities, and a collective blessing ceremony. Through exhibitions, presentations, and hands-on experiences, guests and participants gained a more direct understanding of Taoist beliefs, cultural traditions, and religious practices.

The Yangzhu Taoist Association of America stated that its first anniversary represents both a reflection on the achievements of the past year and the beginning of a new chapter. Looking ahead, the Association will continue to build upon its work in New York, advance the transmission of Taoist religious traditions and culture, and strengthen cooperation with government agencies, international organizations, religious communities, interfaith institutions, and broader society. Through these efforts, the Association seeks to help more people discover and understand Taoism and to further advance Taoist exchange and development in the United States and the international community.
